Join us for a 40-hour sprint featuring challenges spanning Web Exploitation, PWN, Reverse Engineering, Cryptography, Forensics, OSINT, and AI/Prompt Injection across skill levels. events.title: Hacker's Gambit 2026 (Round 1 – Online Qualifier)
events.description: Round 1 – Online Qualifier (48 Hours) The Online Qualifier is the first stage of Hackers Gambit 2026, designed to identify the most skilled cybersecurity teams from around the world. This 48-hour Jeopardy-style Capture The Flag (CTF) competition will challenge participants with a diverse set of real-world cybersecurity problems across multiple domains. Participants will solve challenges in areas including Web Security, Cryptography, Reverse Engineering, Digital Forensics, Binary Exploitation (Pwn), Open Source Intelligence (OSINT), Steganography, and Miscellaneous. Each challenge carries a predefined score based on its difficulty level, and teams earn points by successfully capturing and submitting valid flags. The competition will run continuously for 48 hours, allowing teams to strategize, collaborate, and solve challenges at their own pace within the competition window. A live leaderboard will be available throughout the event (subject to organizer discretion). At the conclusion of the qualifier, participating teams may be required to submit technical write-ups explaining their solutions to selected challenges. These submissions will be reviewed by the organizing committee to verify the authenticity of solutions and ensure fair play. Based on the final scores, write-up evaluation (if applicable), and adherence to the competition rules, the Top 15 teams will qualify for the 24-hour Offline Grand Finale at Jaihind College of Engineering, Kuran, where they will compete for the championship title, prizes, and recognition. Key Highlights Mode: Online Duration: 48 Hours Format: Jeopardy-style Capture The Flag (CTF) Challenge Categories: Web Security, Cryptography, Reverse Engineering, Digital Forensics, Binary Exploitation, OSINT, Steganography, and Miscellaneous Qualification: Top 15 teams advance to the Offline Grand Finale Time: 2 October 2026 (12:00 PM IST) – 4 October 2026 (12:00 PM IST)

events.title: CubeCTF 2026
events.description: CubeCTF is coming back this year with Attack/Defense! Game format will follow traditional FAUST-style A/D format, with infrastructure provided by glitchrange.com. Brush up on your vim shortcuts and tcpdump flags - the environment will be hosted in an isolated environment with only web console access and no direct internet connection to vulnboxes, so AI agents will not have access. If you've been looking to bring the humanity back into CTFs, so have we - come play head-to-head with a range of challenge difficulties designed for everyone. Full infrastructure documentation, rules, and registration information will be published via Discord. Site: https://cubectf.com Discord: https://discord.gg/cRMNjdR4Ug

events.title: CDCTF 2026
events.description: Crimson Defense CTF 2026 will be held on Saturday, October 3rd from 10am to 10pm CDT! CDCTF is a virtual 12-hour Jeopardy-style Capture-the-Flag competition designed for collegiate-level players. All ability levels are welcome. This competition will not only provide satisfying challenges for seasoned players, but be a good introduction to CTFs for new ones! CDCTF is a team competition, you may have up to four participants per team. Universities may have multiple teams representing their school. There will be challenges of all difficulties representing the following categories: Reverse Engineering, Log & Network Traffic Analysis, Forensics, Password Cracking, Cryptography, Open Source Intelligence, Social Engineering, and AI! Registration is OPEN through September 30th CDCTF is hosted and created by Crimson Defense Cyber Security Club at the University of Alabama.

events.title: Hacker's Gambit 2026 (Round 2 – Grand Finale)
events.description: The Grand Finale is the final stage of Hackers Gambit 2026, where the Top 15 teams selected from the Online Qualifier will compete for the championship title. This 24-hour, on-site Capture The Flag (CTF) competition is designed to simulate real-world cybersecurity scenarios and evaluate participants' ability to solve complex security challenges under pressure. Hosted at Jaihind College of Engineering, Kuran, the Grand Finale brings together the highest-performing teams for an intensive competition featuring advanced challenges across multiple cybersecurity domains. Participants will demonstrate their technical expertise, analytical thinking, teamwork, strategic decision-making, and adaptability while competing against some of the best cybersecurity talent. Challenges may cover domains including: Web Security Cryptography Reverse Engineering Digital Forensics Binary Exploitation (Pwn) Open Source Intelligence (OSINT) Steganography Network Security Miscellaneous Challenges Throughout the competition, teams will work continuously for 24 hours, solving progressively challenging problems to accumulate points on the official scoreboard. The competition will conclude with score verification by the organizing committee, followed by the official announcement of winners during the Awards & Closing Ceremony. The Grand Finale provides participants with an opportunity to showcase their cybersecurity skills in a highly competitive environment while networking with industry professionals, sponsors, security researchers, and fellow cybersecurity enthusiasts. events.title: SpookyCTF 2026
events.description: EVENT TIME HAS BEEN SHIFTED TO START AND END 4 HOURS AFTER TIME LISTED ABOVE REGISTRATION IS NOW AVAILABLE! BOO!! Welcome to SpookyCTF 2026! events.title: EyesOpenCTF 7th edition
events.description: EyesOpenCTF 2026 is a FREE CTF competition organized as part of the 7th edition of EOCON. This year, the competition goes far beyond a traditional CTF. You are not simply joining to solve isolated challenges. You are entering The Convergence, a live 48-hour cyber adventure in which reality itself is beginning to fracture. Across more than 40 challenges and 8 disciplines, teams will investigate corrupted systems, recover hidden Reality Fragments, unlock classified dossiers, expose compromised actors, and gradually reconstruct the truth behind a phenomenon threatening the entire world. Every flag matters. Each solved challenge can reveal new intelligence, unlock characters and locations, alter the mission briefing, and move the story forward in real time. The competition platform becomes a living investigation that evolves with the progress of the Operators. Expect : - web exploitation, - digital forensics, - reverse engineering, - binary exploitation, - cryptography, - OSINT, - AI security, and more—woven into a single coherent mission unlike any previous EyesOpenCTF. Built for teams from around the world and open to different experience levels, EyesOpenCTF is both a proving ground and an immersive narrative experience where competitors can learn, compete, get noticed, and join a fast-growing international cybersecurity community. As part of EOCON, the competition also connects participants with experts, researchers, recruiters, entrepreneurs, and emerging talent from Africa and beyond. It is a place where technical ability meets storytelling, where discoveries change the mission, and where tomorrow’s collaborations, careers, and opportunities begin. Form your team. Enter the Protocol. Recover the Fragments. events.description: Outback Overflow is a free online jeopardy-style CTF built for high schoolers across Australia. Run by the High School Cybersecurity Community, it's designed to be a stepping stone for students getting into cyber security, whether you've never touched a terminal or you're already popping shells. Our goal is simple: grow the number of young people in cyber security and give Australian high schoolers a CTF they can call their own. events.title: Seize da Flaq
events.description: Seize Da Flaq is the flagship national-level Capture The Flag (CTF) competition organized by Cyberonites Club, GLA University. events.title: Crate-CTF 2026
events.description: Crate-CTF is an annual Capture The Flag (CTF) competition organised by the Swedish Defence Research Agency in collaboration with the Swedish Armed Forces, designed to introduce high school and university students to the field of cybersecurity. This year we return for our seventh CTF, with challenges for all skill levels from beginners to seasoned CTF players. The challenges are categorised into web exploitation, reverse engineering, binary exploitation, cryptography, forensics, OSINT, networking and the all-encompassing "other". While the event will be conducted in Swedish, international participants are also welcome to join (using translation tools as needed). Communication with challenge authors and administrators can be conducted in English.

events.title: CyberSci Regional Qualifiers 2026-27
events.description: CyberSci is Canada's national Cyber Security Challenge for university and college students. - Think you've got an elite team of students? Come and prove it. Our winners will go on to compete against the best in the world. - Just starting out? This is the best way to learn and rise to the top. - Annual in-person events since 2016. (Online during Covid.) Over 500 students so far. Format: - Modified jeopardy style. Realistic IT environment. - Regional qualifiers are held in Nov-Dec each year. - National finals are the following July. - Winning teams represent Canada at international events in the Fall. For Regionals (qualifiers): We do hacking in the morning, interviews in the afternoon, and job offers by supper (for intern/summer/coop jobs). - Full-time job offers take a few more days. - Students register their team through their school instructor or computer club. Max 2 teams per school. For nationals: Participants will be the winning team from each regional/qualifier - PLUS one all-juniors (19 and under) - AND one all-women team (chosen from participants at the Regionals). Two-day event.

events.title: BlackHat MEA CTF Final 2026
events.description: Black Hat MEA Capture The Flag (CTF) 2026 ? The Black Hat MEA Capture The Flag (CTF) is the largest cybersecurity competition in the region and officially the largest Capture The Flag competition in the world, recognized with a Guinness World Record. Organized by the Saudi Federation for Cybersecurity, Programming and Drones (SAFCSP) in collaboration with Black Hat MEA, the competition brings together thousands of cybersecurity professionals, researchers, students, and enthusiasts from around the globe. Powered by the FlagYard platform, the competition follows a Jeopardy-style format, where teams of 3–5 players compete across a range of cybersecurity challenges, including Web Exploitation, PWN, Digital Forensics, Reverse Engineering, Cryptography, and AI Hacking. Competition Timeline Registration: June 3 – August 29, 2026 Online Qualifiers: August 29, 2026 | 10:00 AM KSA (GMT+3) | Online Thousands of participants will compete globally in teams of 3–5 members, with the top 150 teams qualifying for the final stage. On-site Finals The top 150 teams will be invited to Riyadh, Saudi Arabia for a 3-day final competition during Black Hat MEA, taking place from December 1–3, 2026. Register Now: https://flagyard.com/events/3468f495-a92c-498b-90c2-994dfb99ea0b Support: blackhatctf@safcsp.org.sa
